subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB352; PB353. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR21): 'If LAST is specified, the file position indicator is set to the record number of the last existing logical record in the physical file. If no records exist in the file, or the physical file does not support the ability to position at the last record, the I-O status value ... is set to 23, the invalid key condition exists, and the execution of the START statement is unsuccessful.' Same absence as GR20 and the same single site: KeyedIoBinder.BindStart rejects every sequential-organization START before the FIRST/LAST discrimination is ever reached, SequentialConnector implements no positioning entry point, and FileRegistry.StartFirstLast has no sequential arm. OBSERVED (probe/seq-start/STPRB2.cob): `START SQF LAST` compiles clean and the run unit dies on the preceding `START SQF FIRST` with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException — neither form ever executes. Expected from GR21 for that program (three records AAA-1, BBB-2, CCC-3): the file position indicator is set to record number 3, status '00', and the next sequential READ makes 'CCC-3' available. Note that GR21 also requires the '23' + invalid-key answer when the physical file cannot position at the last record — a sequential host stream is exactly the case the rule anticipates, so an implementation that cannot seek backwards is still obliged to answer '23' rather than abort. See findings M1 and M2. EDITIONS: as GR20.

LANDED 2026-09-05 (kb/Work PB352). The LAST twin of GR20, same sites. MEASURED against the rule in conformance:cases/9.1.13.5-Invalid-key-condition-with-unsuccessful-completion/pb352_start_sequential_first_last on the very program the adjudication predicted from (three records AAA-1 / BBB-2 / CCC-3): `START SQF LAST` reports SL=00 and the next sequential READ makes R3=CCC-3 available - the record NUMBER of the last existing logical record, reached by scanning the frames rather than by guessing a byte offset, so a short final block and a line-sequential file behave the same way (LL-OK, LSL=00, LR1=L-3). With no records: EL-INV, EL=23.

PB353 (2026-09-06) - THE EDITION-GATE HALF OF THE SAME RULE. PB352 landed the behaviour and, in doing so, moved the FIRST/LAST arm above the sequential bail-out, which incidentally closed this note's own repro: `START SQF FIRST` at --std 85 now reports COBOL0900 (measured on the current tree, both the sequential and the relative program). The GENERAL shape it named was still live, and on this very statement: the gate keyed on BoundKeyedStart.Mode, so EVERY OTHER path that returns before the node is built still dropped it. Measured at --std 85 before the fix - `START NOSUCHF FIRST` -> COBOL1639 alone; `START SDF FIRST` on an SD -> COBOL1692 alone. FIRST and LAST are one construct (14.9.41.2 prints one general format) and 14.9.41.3 SR2 makes the phrase mandatory on a sequential file rather than different there, so the introduction cannot depend on anything the binder resolves: the gate now fires on RECOGNITION in the VersionConformancePass parse arm (VisitStartStatement), and KeyedIoBinder holds no edition gate of any kind. The four sibling gates on the same shape moved with it (START WITH LENGTH, READ PREVIOUS, READ ADVANCING ON LOCK, INVOKE). EditionGateArmDriftTests keeps the assignment true: it derives both arms from the pass source and requires every bound-arm construct to name the resolved fact that keeps it there, and it recompiles every gated construct's own constructs.json program with the procedure-division operands broken, requiring the edition diagnostic to outlive the bind. The rule's own behaviour is unchanged - GR20/GR21 still hold through conformance:cases/9.1.13.5-Invalid-key-condition-with-unsuccessful-completion/pb352_start_sequential_first_last.
